question.knowledge_point: Computing the Area Scale Factor of a Linear Transformation
question.problem:
What is the area scale factor of the linear transformation $T$ that is given by its standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}8 & 5 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}]?
$$
question.worked_solution:
The area scale factor of a linear transformation $T$ with standard matrix $T$ is equal to $|det(T)|.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}|det(T)| & =|8\cdot 3-5\cdot (-2)| \\  & =|24+10| \\  & =34.\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Calculating the Area of the Image of an Object Under a Linear Transformation Given a Diagram
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13992537/assets/4f31b9f180b1b766451685428fc289766832fe5d0c7d8902a601ebf060eab0e7.png)

Consider the shaded region $D$ shown above. What is the area of the image of $D$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ with the standard matrix $T,$ given below?

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that for any linear transformation $T,$ we have the following connection between the area of $D$ and the area of the image $T(D)$ under the action of $T:$

$$
\text{Area}(T(D))=|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D).
$$

From the diagram, we have

$$
\text{Area}(D)=\pi \cdot {2}^{2}=4\pi .
$$

Computing the determinant of $T,$ we get 

$$
det(T)=(-2)\cdot 5-(-1)\cdot 0=-10.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(D)) & =|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =|-10|\cdot 4\pi  \\  & =40\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
